title: Fast Enzymatic Processing of Proteins for MS Detection with a Flow-through Microreactor
protocol: Cut the 100 µm internal diameter x 360 µm outer diameter capillary to a length of 7-8 cm with the glass capillary cleaver.
Verify under the microscope that both capillary ends have a clean, straight cut without any protruding burrs.
Insert the 20 µm ID x 90 µm OD capillary into one end of the 100 µm ID x 360 µm OD capillary for a length of ~6 mm; observe this operation under a microscope if necessary.
Apply a small droplet of glue E6000 around the junction of the 90 µm OD/100 µm ID capillaries with the end of a Q-tip.
Let the glue cure overnight at room temperature.
Cut the inserted 20 µm ID x 90 µm OD capillary to a length of ~10-15 mm; this will be the electrospray ionization emitter.
Pre-cut the 1/32" OD PEEK, 1/16" OD PEEK and 1/16" OD PTFE tubing in pieces of 4-5 cm in length.
Connect the opposite end of the 100 µm ID x 360 µm OD capillary to a PEEK union.
Use a 1/32" PEEK sleeve for providing a leak-free connection.
Insert/tighten a piece of ~5 cm long 1/16" PTFE tubing into the opposite end of the union.
Weigh approximately 4 mg of C18 (5 µm) particles in a pre-cleaned/dried 2 ml glass vial.
Add 0.5 ml isopropanol to the vial and close it.
Disperse the slurry in an ultrasonicator bath.
Withdraw approximately 200 μl of the slurry with a 250 µl syringe.
Insert the syringe needle into the 1/16" PTFE tubing of the PEEK union.
Dispense slowly the slurry into the 100 µm ID x 360 µm OD capillary.
Observe under the microscope as the capillary fills with particles until a length of 2-3 mm packing is achieved.
Rinse the microreactor with approximately 50 μl solution of H2O/CH3CN (50:50 v/v).
Rinse the microreactor again with approximately 50 µl solution of H2O/CH3CN (98:2 v/v).
Rinse glass vials and polypropylene tubes in a fume hood.
Prepare 10 ml of a solution of H2O/CH3CN (98:2 v/v) by mixing 9.8 ml H2O with 200 µl CH3CN.
Mix the solution by sonication.
Prepare 10 ml of a solution of H2O/CH3CN (50:50 v/v) by mixing 5 ml H2O with 5 ml CH3CN.
Mix this solution by sonication.
Prepare 4 ml of an acidified aqueous solution (TFA 0.01% v/v) by adding 4 µl TFA(10%) to 4 ml H2O/CH3CN (98:2 v/v).
Mix the acidified solution by sonication.
Prepare 4 ml of an acidified organic solution by adding 4 µl TFA (10%) to 4 ml H2O/CH3CN (50:50 v/v) in a 4 ml glass vial; mix by sonication.
Weigh 16 mg NH4HCO3 with an analytical microbalance in a 4 ml glass vial; add 4 ml of the H2O/CH3CN (98:2 v/v) solution and disperse by sonication to result in a 50 mM solution of NH4HCO3.
Weigh 5 mg of a standard protein with an analytical microbalance in a 4 ml glass vial; add 4 ml DI water and disperse by sonication.
Prepare 1 ml protein solution (1-2 µM) by diluting the high µM-level concentration solution with NH4HCO3 (50 mM) aqueous buffer; mix by sonication.
Prepare the trypsin solution (5 µM) by dissolving 20 µg sequencing-grade trypsin in 170 µl NH4HCO3 (50 mM) aqueous buffer; disperse by sonication.
Disconnect the capillary microreactor from the PEEK union and connect to the PEEK Tee.
Insert a ~2 cm long Pt wire in the side-arm of the PEEK Tee using a 1/32" PEEK sleeve for providing a leak-free connection.
Connect a 50 µm ID x 360 µm OD (~0.5 m long) sample transfer capillary to the opposite end of the PEEK Tee.
Use a 1/32" PEEK sleeve for providing a leak-free connection.
Secure the PEEK Tee on the XYZ-stage.
Position the ESI emitter ~2 mm away from the mass spectrometer inlet capillary.
Connect the Pt wire to the ESI power supply source of the mass spectrometer.
Connect the opposite end of the sample transfer capillary to the stainless steel union.
Use a 1/16" PEEK sleeve for providing a leak-free connection.
Connect a 4-5 cm long 1/16" PTFE tubing to the opposite end of the stainless steel union.
Insert the 250 µl syringe needle in the PTFE tubing.
Turn on the pump and set the flow rate at the desired value (e.g., 2 µl/min).
Input tandem MS data acquisition parameters into the software package that controls the MS instrument.
Save as a method file to ready the setup for performing the analysis.
Prepare a microfluidic device from glass or polymeric substrates.
Connect a microreactor (1) with an inlet (2), outlet (3), and side port (4).
Insert interconnecting channels for fluidic manipulations (~110 µm wide, ~50 µm deep).
Create a multichannel structure (5) consisting of 1.5-2 µm deep x 10 μm wide x 100 μm long microchannels.
Place the multichannel structure 25 µm apart to act as a filter for retaining particles in the microreactor.
Glue specialized connectors to the inlet ports or devise a polymeric stand with fittings for fluid delivery.
Prepare a slurry of C18 particles (5 µm).
Deliver the slurry to the microreactor using a syringe connected via 1/16" PTFE tubing to the chip side port (4).
Seal the side port after particle loading with epoxy glue and cure for 1 hour in an oven at 90°C.
Insert a capillary (20 µm ID x 90 µm OD x 10 mm length) into the outlet port, seal with E6000 glue, and let cure overnight.
Connect a 50 µm ID x 360 µm OD (~0.5 m long) sample transfer capillary to the chip inlet port (2).
Attach the opposite end of the capillary to a 250 µl syringe and connect it to a syringe pump.
Place a light-weight PEEK Tee connector on the sample transfer line just prior to the inlet port.
Insert a Pt wire on the side-arm of the Tee as the ESI electrode.
Secure the microfluidic device on the XYZ stage with the ESI emitter positioned ~2 mm away from the mass spectrometer inlet capillary.
Rinse the microreactor by infusing an aqueous solution of NH4HCO3 (50 mM) in H2O/CH3CN (98:2 v/v) at 2 µl/min for 5 min.
Load the protein sample (1 µM) on the microreactor by infusing the sample solution at 2 µl/min for 5 min.
Infuse the trypsin solution (5 µM) over the adsorbed protein on the microreactor at 2 µl/min for 1-3 min.
Quench the proteolytic digestion process by rinsing the microreactor with an acidified aqueous solution of TFA (0.01% v/v) in H2O/CH3CN (98:2 v/v) at 2 µl/min for 5 min.
Start eluting the protein digest from the microreactor by infusing an acidified organic solution of TFA (0.01% v/v) in H2O/CH3CN (50:50 v/v) at 8 μl/h.
Turn on the MS data acquisition process and the ESI voltage (~2,000 V).
Acquire MS data using the specified parameters.
Observe the elution of the tryptic peptides.
Process tandem MS data with a search engine compatible with the raw MS data format.
Process LTQ-MS raw files using an organism-specific minimally redundant protein database.
Upload the raw data in the search engine.
Set parent and fragment ion mass tolerances to 2 and 1 Da, respectively.
Use only fully tryptic fragments with up to two missed cleavages for the search.
Filter the data to select only high-confidence peptide matches to proteins in the database.
Evaluate protein and peptide-level results.
